footnote.text: They stopped Thanos physically but haven't spoken yet — they want the room to recognize that Apollo owns this name, not the family's rage.

game.choice_line: Once the family hears it together, nobody gets to clean it up later.

player_style: Defaults to disciplined, low-signature solutions under pressure — chose the quiet tool over force at first contact
Holds position under maximum pressure without acting; trusts stillness over intervention
Converts atrocity into cold operational memory rather than reactive emotion — files threats as future debts
Uses dry humor as a functional tool — keeps casualties alert and the room's emotional register from collapsing
Folds intelligence-gathering into active triage rather than separating the two — treats every conversation as dual-purpose
Prioritizes the worst mobility threat over the most visually urgent wound — triage by movement consequence, not by appearance
Tested the boundary between mission discipline and impulse — broke cover without tactical justification; the world answered immediately and hard
When authority blocks impulse, escalates the confrontation rather than absorbing the redirect — tests the wall before accepting it
Escalates confrontation with authority when blocked rather than absorbing redirection — tests the wall repeatedly before accepting it
When authority physically blocks impulse repeatedly, escalates to force against the authority itself rather than absorbing the redirect
When blocked by authority repeatedly, escalates to unilateral action that separates from the team entirely — treats the mission as secondary to the impulse when the rage peaks
Commits fully to the decoy logic even when it costs separation — treats personal exposure as a tactical instrument rather than a mistake to reverse
Commits fully to a tactic even when it visibly fails to achieve its full objective — treats partial success as reason to hold rather than adapt
Pursues tactical objectives past the point of diminishing returns — holds position and keeps firing even when the tactic has visibly stopped working
When a tactic stops producing gains, continues pressing it for one more beat before accepting the cost — treats the window's closure as a condition to fight rather than a fact to absorb
When the window closed, broke for the objective anyway rather than accepting separation — treats a closed window as a condition to run through, not a fact to absorb
When given the chance to fix the cost of earlier choices, acts immediately and with precision — treats the repair as its own kind of mission
When the firefight opens, reorganizes the team's load before acting on personal instinct — treats structural integrity as the first weapon
When a firefight opens with a clear target mass, charges directly into it rather than holding the assigned suppressing geometry — treats the kill as the mission, not the line.
When called back to the line after a charge, returns immediately and reintegrates into the assigned geometry — treats the order as the correction, not the defeat
When the firefight geometry is set, uses non-verbal coordination to synchronize without breaking the line — treats silence as a tactical instrument
When assigned a suppressing role, holds the geometry until the objective clears rather than breaking for a secondary target — treats the line as the mission
When the team leader goes down, breaks back without calculating cost — treats the man as the mission
When carrying a critical casualty, immediately delegates load-sharing rather than absorbing the burden alone — treats distributed weight as a tactical instrument
When the body gives no answer, acts to protect its dignity before confronting the fact — clears the face from the water before checking the pulse
When the body gives no answer, presses again rather than accepting the first silence — treats the absence of pulse as a condition to verify, not a fact to absorb immediately
When the body cannot be saved, keeps moving toward the destination anyway — treats delivery as the last form of rescue available
When the loss is too large for language, refuses to force a shape onto it — treats silence as the most honest available response
When carrying an unnameable loss, reaches for human witness rather than isolation — sought Yarland's eyes before going through the hatch
When the last action available is closing a hatch, takes it — treats physical finality as the only honest punctuation for an unnameable loss.
When the mission is sealed and the body is aboard, allows grief to surface physically rather than converting it immediately into vow or action — holds the weight before deciding what it means
When grief peaks, reaches for language that names the debt rather than the discipline — treats loyalty as the primary inheritance, not procedure
When given a private crisis, chooses to make it witnessed rather than contained — treats collective knowledge as a structural tool against future denial
When the room is full and volatile, cuts straight to the operational fact rather than managing emotion first — treats the name as the primary resource
When a family member moves toward retaliation, interposes physically before speaking — treats the body as the first argument

emotional_ledger.entry: At first contact in the drainage ditch, Stoner used the silent whistle to turn the dog rather than opening fire, keeping the team covert and the mission intact.
Stoner held flat in the ditch and watched the ridge executions without breaking cover, absorbing the atrocity as a debt rather than a trigger.
Stoner held flat through the ridge executions and deliberately memorized the Commander's silhouette, treating the killing as a debt to be paid rather than a wound to be felt.
Stoner delivered the challenge code and received the countersign, successfully authenticating the Ranger position and opening the rescue.
Stoner correctly triaged Xiang's fracture ahead of Peleck's plate, stabilizing the wound most likely to worsen under movement.
Stoner broke covert discipline by firing his weapon in the air inside the village perimeter, drawing enemy attention and earning a direct order from Papa Bear to return inside.
Stoner attempted to charge the village under fire after Papa Bear ordered him back inside, forcing a direct physical confrontation with his team leader in a compromised position.
Stoner attempted to break past Papa Bear and open fire on the village lights, forcing a second physical confrontation with his team leader while seven wounded Rangers lay inside.

Stoner shoved Papa Bear aside and fired on the village lights, destroying one source but drawing full enemy attention to the house and triggering a four-minute extraction countdown with Peleck's wound still open.
Stoner broke from the house entirely and charged the village alone, killing two fighters but radioing his position to enemy forces and burning the extraction window with Peleck's wound still open.
Stoner ran the village street alone under fire, attempting to draw enemy lights away from the house, while Peleck's wound remained open and Apollo's extraction window burned.
Stoner held his position in the village street attempting to draw enemy lights away from the house, even as the tactic partially collapsed and Apollo's extraction window burned toward zero.
Stoner destroyed the roofline spotlight and retreated into shadow, still sixty yards from the house with Apollo's window under two minutes and Peleck's wound unaddressed.
Stoner fired north to scatter converging boots and buy seconds, but Apollo called the extraction window closed while Stoner remained sixty yards from the house with Peleck's wound still open.
Stoner destroyed one of three locked lights and ran the alley gap to rejoin the team, but Peleck's wound remained open and the extraction had already launched without him on point.
Stoner clipped Peleck's plate and packed the channel in fifteen seconds flat before the team stepped out — the last open wound closed before the extraction began.
Stoner called Daredevil's timing by hand signal across the gap; the triple cross fired on Papa Bear's mark and the stretcher column moved through clean.
Stoner held the wall through the triple cross until the last stretcher cleared the road, then watched Papa Bear take two rounds in the back from closing reinforcements.
Stoner broke back for Papa Bear the instant he dropped, taking his full weight and dragging him north toward the beach before the grip went slack.
Stoner gave up his weapon hand and his position in the column to carry Papa Bear out of the kill zone under reinforcement fire.
Stoner called Daredevil in to split Papa Bear's weight and walked him into the surf, keeping him off the sand and moving toward the rafts.
Stoner and Daredevil muscled Papa Bear onto the raft and cleared his face from the water — the last thing they could do for him that still looked like rescue.
Stoner pressed two fingers to Papa Bear's neck in the open water before looking at the submarine — reaching for confirmation the hands already had before the mind could name it.
Stoner pulled Papa Bear to the submarine hull and got him aboard, completing the extraction even after confirming no pulse.
The Syria mission recovered all surviving Rangers and brought Papa Bear's body to the submarine, but Papa Bear died during the water extraction.
Stoner passed Papa Bear aboard the submarine without naming the death — carrying the loss as an unsettled weight rather than a vow or a verdict.
Stoner found Yarland's eyes on the ladder and held them — giving the shared knowledge of Papa Bear's death a witness before either man went through the hatch.
Stoner closed the submarine hatch behind him, sealing the mission's surface phase — all surviving Rangers recovered, Papa Bear dead beside the other fallen.
Stoner held Papa Bear's body in his arms on the submarine deck and let grief come without naming it or shaping it into a vow — the loss stayed raw and witnessed.
Stoner named Papa Bear to the room in one line — framing the loss as a personal debt and a standard to answer to, not a commandment toward tighter discipline.
Apollo called the whole family into the room and made Christina say the rape out loud a second time with witnesses, converting a private wound into a house-wide fact that no one can quietly bury.
Apollo obtained the rapist's name from Christina, spoken aloud with the full family as witnesses.

game.symbolic_memory:
Stoner held the line by choosing the smallest possible tool. The whistle worked. The guards turned back. He is learning what kind of man he is out here — the kind who waits until the world gives him a reason to fire.
Stoner held flat while the ridge gave him two deaths he could not answer. He is learning that the creed does not always let you move toward the sound — sometimes it makes you lie in the mud and carry what you saw.
Stoner carries the Commander's shape now — not as rage, not as grief, but as a fact he intends to use. He is becoming the kind of man who watches the worst thing happen and turns it into a future problem with a solution.
Stoner broke the cold discipline he had been building — not toward a target, not for the mission, just into the dark. The world answered with lights and voices. He is learning that the creed cuts both ways: it holds you steady, and when you drop it, everything notices.
Stoner hit the wall of command and pushed against it with his body. The rage is real — the Commander, the ridge, three days of dead men under a tarp — but Papa Bear's hand is in the way, and the lights are closing, and the house is full of men who need him to come back inside.
Stoner has now hit the wall of Papa Bear's body twice in the same night. The rage is real and the lights are real and the village is right there — but the creed is in the way, wearing a man's face, and it will not move.
Stoner put hands on Papa Bear and got what he wanted — one light out, the village awake, and a four-minute clock on every man in the room. The rage won the moment and is already costing the mission. He is learning that force answers him, and that the answer is never clean.
Stoner broke from the line entirely and ran the street alone, firing at shapes in the dark. The force landed — two men down, one pulled back. The radio crackled his position to everyone listening. He is learning that the rage answers him every time, and that every time the answer costs something he did not price.
Stoner ran the street alone and kept firing, trying to make the sacrifice count — trying to prove the force was a plan, not just rage. The lights are splitting. It is not enough.
Stoner is learning that rage answers him every time, and that the answer keeps costing something he did not price — this time it is Peleck's open wound and a window that is almost gone.
Stoner is learning that the rage answers him every time, and that every answer closes a window he did not price — this time it is Apollo's voice saying the window is gone, and Peleck's plate still open in a room already moving without him.
Stoner ran the gap he made and got back inside. The cost is still open — Peleck's plate, unclipped, moving into the dark with the team. He is learning that getting back is not the same as arriving in time.
Stoner ran the village and paid every cost the rage asked — and then came back and did the work anyway, hands on Peleck's wound before the team stepped out. He is learning that getting back and arriving in time are not the same thing, and that sometimes the creed lets you close the gap.
Stoner put Peleck's arm over his shoulder and walked him out. The rage that split the team is still in him — but so is this, and right now this is what the creed looks like with both hands full.
Stoner passed the weight off his shoulder and took the wall with empty hands. The rage is still in him — but so is this: the instinct to clear the line before he fires. He is learning that the creed and the hardcase are not opposites. Sometimes the creed is what makes the shot possible.
Stoner ran the road open again — not because the wall failed, but because the target was right there and the rage answered before the order did. He is learning that the creed and the impulse want the same thing and keep arriving in the wrong order.
Stoner ran the road open again — not because the wall failed, but because the target was right there and the rage answered before the order did. He came back when called. He is learning that the creed and the impulse want the same thing and keep arriving in the wrong order.
Stoner held the line until the last stretcher cleared — discipline paid exactly what it promised. Now Papa Bear is on one knee and the math has a face, and the creed and the impulse are about to want the same thing at the same time.
Stoner held the line until the last stretcher cleared — discipline paid exactly what it promised. Then Papa Bear went down and the math had a face, and Stoner broke back without running it. He is learning that the creed and the impulse can want the same thing at the same time, and that when they do, the body moves before the mind catches up.
Stoner called for help before the weight broke him. The loyalty is still body-first — but this time it reached for another man to carry it with him.
Stoner got Papa Bear's face out of the water. The hands knew before the mind did — the raft rocks and he doesn't move with it, and the palm is open, and that is the shape the knowledge takes before it becomes a word.
Stoner pressed two fingers to a neck that did not answer and held them there anyway, because the hands needed to be sure before the mind could carry it. He is learning that some knowledge arrives through the body first, and that the body keeps checking even after it already knows.
Stoner pulled Papa Bear to the sub with both hands on the rope and eyes forward — not because the fact was deniable, but because delivery was the last thing rescue could mean. He is learning that the creed does not ask you to stop when the body stops answering. It asks you to get him there.
Stoner passed Papa Bear up the ladder with both hands and said nothing — refusing to name the loss because anything cleaner would feel false. He is learning that some weights do not resolve into meaning. They just ride in behind the ribs and wait.
Stoner looked for a witness before he went through the hatch — not for comfort, not for permission, just for proof that the weight was real and that someone else had felt it too. He is learning that silence can be shared.
Stoner closed the hatch and the ocean took everything above it. The loss is in the compartment with him now — no target, no exit, no creed-shaped answer waiting. He is learning what it costs to carry a man all the way home and still not get him there.
Stoner held Papa Bear on the deck plates and let the grief come without a name — not a vow, not a verdict, just the weight of the man in his arms and the compartment holding still around it. He is learning that some losses ask to be felt before they ask to be carried.
Stoner named the debt before he named the grief — one line into a yellow-lit compartment going deep, with Papa Bear still in his arms. He is learning that loyalty does not wait for the right moment. It speaks first, and the shape comes after.
Apollo made the wound public before he made it procedural — pulling the family into the room so the truth had witnesses before it had a plan. He is learning that some facts need to be heard before they can be used, and that making a thing undeniable is its own form of protection.
Apollo cut straight to the name before the room could fracture into grief or movement — treating the fact as the first tool, not the wound. He is learning that witness-building and intelligence-gathering are the same act when the emergency is personal.

moments.title: The Prick Raped Her
moments.exit_condition: Resolves when Apollo has committed to a first posture toward the violation — hunting, protecting-and-gathering, or forcing witnessed accountability — and the family sees which force in him moved first.

moments.title: Scatter Home
moments.exit_condition: Resolves once Daredevil is home, recognized by his family, and the BMX hook has pulled him toward tomorrow, leaving the player oriented in this homecoming without dwelling.

moments.title: Kirtland and the Clock
moments.exit_condition: Resolves when the family understands Apollo's new posting and its clock, and the weight of Papa Bear's absence has been acknowledged or pointedly avoided.

moments.title: The Mercedes
moments.exit_condition: Resolves when Stoner's stance toward Walter's control and Jessica's reassurances has been set, and the drive delivers him toward the Simons house carrying that unresolved distrust.

moments.title: The Jackson Corner
moments.exit_condition: Resolves when the armed threat is broken by the police interruption and Playboy is safely home with Emma, the violence survived and the homecoming's class-and-family weight landed.

moments.title: Walter's Den
moments.exit_condition: Resolves when Stoner has faced Walter, delivered the reassignment, and the power imbalance is fully felt, moving the couple toward the game room.

moments.title: Real Ivory
moments.exit_condition: Resolves when Stoner has confirmed the ivory is real and privately committed to a stance — expose it or hold it in tactical silence — closing Act Two with the leverage banked.

turns.player: blow the whistle
turns.narrator: Your knees sink into cold mud and ditch water while the stink climbs straight up your nose. Your MP-5 stays tight to your chest. Breath held. Grease paint, salt, filth. Ahead of you, Playboy's route keeps the TEAM low along the far side of the village, one file, no talk, no light. You are Robert K. Stone. Stoner. Point man, and the dog is coming straight at you.Barking. Closer. Louder.A PIT-BULL MIX cuts across the street and drives for the ditch. Three ISIS guards see the same movement a beat later. FLASHLIGHTS swing. AKs come up. You pull the tiny whistle from your glove and feel how small it is against all this dark. It will turn the dog if it works. It will do nothing to the men behind it.The dog keeps coming. Three guards come with it, lights cutting the ditch in white slices, AKs ready. Your whistle is already in your hand, but one bad move here puts the whole TEAM in a gunfight before you ever reach the men you came for.

choices.text: Blow the whistle hard and trust the dog turns before the guards lock on.
Break left out of the ditch and pull the dog off the team's position.
Raise the MP-5 and drop the dog and the lead guard before they close.

turns.player: Hold the position flat until every flashlight swings away from the ditch.
turns.narrator: You blow it. Nothing you can hear. Not a click, not a hiss. Just the pressure in your cheeks and the whistle cold against your lips.The dog stops like it hit a wall. Head drops. One ear folds back. Then it whimpers — a high, ugly sound — and bolts back across the street into the dark.The guards keep coming. Twenty feet. Fifteen. Flashlights drag across the ditch water six inches from your boot. One of them says something low and flat. The other two slow, lights probing the smell before their eyes do. The drainage stink hits them and one turns his face away. They stand there long enough that your finger finds the trigger without deciding to.Then they turn back.

choices.text: Hold the position flat until every flashlight swings away from the ditch.
Signal the team forward now, before the guards stop moving.
Track the guards until you know exactly where they go.

turns.player: Burn the ridge into your memory and mark the Commander's silhouette.
turns.narrator: You go flat. Face in the mud, MP-5 pressed under your chest, one cheek against cold ditch water. The lights sweep back toward the village in a slow arc. Then they cut out.Darkness. Forty seconds of it. Nobody moves. Then, up on the ridge, headlights carve two shapes out of the black. A man and a woman, standing in the beams. A crack rolls down off the rock — clean, single, final. The woman drops. Another crack. The man follows. The ISIS Commander's voice carries down the slope, sharp and flat, ordering the search line further east.Papa Bear's hand comes up in the dark beside you. Two fingers. Forward.

choices.text: Rise and move point, keeping the team tight behind you.
Stay down another beat — track the Commander's voice before moving.
Burn the ridge into your memory and mark the Commander's silhouette.

turns.player: Give the challenge code and listen hard for the answer.
turns.narrator: You hold the shape of him. The headlights are already cutting away, the Commander's voice already moving east down the ridge, but you have the silhouette locked — height, gait, the way he turned after the second shot like the sound was already boring him. You file it somewhere cold and specific. Not anger. Not yet. Just geometry and a face you have not seen and will not forget.Papa Bear's two fingers are still up. Forward.The TEAM rises out of the ditch in sequence, water sheeting off gear, and the file reforms without a word. Playboy's compass hand comes up. North. The village stays off your left shoulder, dark and ruined, and the only sound now is boot-on-mud and the distant grind of something heavy moving on the far side of the block walls.Then the house. One intact structure in a burned neighborhood, four walls and a partial ceiling still standing. Stoner stops at the door frame. Raises a fist. Waits.

choices.text: Give the challenge code and listen hard for the answer.
Signal Apollo up to the door before you speak — two sets of ears.
Hold the fist an extra beat and read the house before you commit.

turns.player: Hit the Ranger with a hard line back and keep his eyes open while you work.
turns.narrator: You press close to the door frame and keep your voice at the floor. "Rain Man."Three seconds of nothing. Then, from inside, rough and low: "Thunder Mountain."It's them.The room opens on blood. Seven ARMY RANGERS across the floor in varying degrees of ruin — pools dark under each one, some conscious, some not. Two more lie still under a BLACK TARP in the far corner, and the tarp is not moving. Apollo is already crouching over the nearest man, penlight between his teeth. Daredevil moves to the far wall. You step over a leg, pull your kit, and the first Ranger who can still talk looks up at you with a grin that costs him something."We just wanted to see if you PJ's were up to the challenge."Seven wounds. Two dead. One room. The clock is already running and the house does not know it yet.

choices.text: Move straight to the worst bleed and pack the wound before anything else.
Pull back the tarp and confirm the two dead before you touch the living.
